# Clear Creek County

> Paid camping is 'Commercial Camping', allowed only in C-OR (up to 50 sites), C-TR or a Planned Development. 1-50 sites get an administrative permit. Sites must be 100 ft from existing homes, with access from a county-maintained road.

## Planning & zoning

- Department: <https://www.co.clear-creek.co.us/124/Planning>

## Private (non-commercial) camping

- Private camping means no money or thing of value is exchanged. Allowed 14 days per year with no permit, plus 30 more days with a Private Camping Permit (approved sanitation required). Longer needs a Special Use Permit. — [[1]](https://www.clearcreekcounty.us/DocumentCenter/View/10359/Section_21) *(verified)*
- A new Private Camping Permit can't be issued until 30 days after the previous one expired. — [[1]](https://www.clearcreekcounty.us/DocumentCenter/View/10359/Section_21) *(verified)*

## Paid camping / campground pathway

- Commercial Camping (money or value exchanged) is allowed only in Commercial-Outdoor Recreation (C-OR, max 50 sites), Commercial-Tourism Recreation (C-TR), or a Planned Development that includes it. — [[1]](https://www.clearcreekcounty.us/DocumentCenter/View/10359/Section_21) *(verified)*
- 1-50 sites: Minor Camping Permit (administrative). 51+ sites: Major Camping Permit (public review). — [[1]](https://www.clearcreekcounty.us/DocumentCenter/View/10359/Section_21) *(verified)*
- Standards: nothing within 100 ft of an existing residence; 50 ft from streams (100 ft for structures/sanitary facilities); max 20 sites/acre; legal access from a county-maintained public road; animal-proof trash; no campgrounds in the 100-year floodplain; max 30 days per party per year. — [[1]](https://www.clearcreekcounty.us/DocumentCenter/View/10359/Section_21) *(verified)*

> County "camping on your own land" rules usually cover **non-commercial** use by the owner and their guests.
> A paid Hipcamp booking is often a campground or commercial use instead. Ask Planning in writing:
> *"How do you classify paid overnight camping booked through an online platform on this parcel?"*

## RVs, tiny homes & structures

- Not confirmed. Most Colorado counties treat RVs as temporary/recreational, not dwellings. See [Structures, Tiny Homes & RVs](../09-structures-tiny-homes-rvs.md).
- County building department (or the town's inside town limits). Confirm the adopted code edition, and the wildfire resiliency code if the parcel is in the WUI.

## Short-term rental / lodging rules

- Not researched. If you offer a cabin, yurt or other structure, check for an STR/vacation-rental permit.
- Lodging taxes: Hipcamp collects state, county lodging and local marketing district taxes. Check for a **home-rule city** tax if the parcel is inside a municipality. See [Taxes](../10-taxes-and-licensing.md).

## Health, fire & other authorities

- Septic (OWTS), privies, water systems: the county's local public health agency. Find it at [CDPHE: find your local public health agency](https://cdphe.colorado.gov/public-information/find-your-local-public-health-agency).
- Fire bans: the Board of County Commissioners by ordinance, enforced by the Sheriff ([C.R.S. 30-15-401](https://law.justia.com/codes/colorado/title-30/county-powers-and-functions/general/article-15/part-4/section-30-15-401/)). A fire protection district may add restrictions.
- Wells: a Colorado Division of Water Resources permit, with uses limited to what the permit lists. See [Water & Wells](../07-water-and-wells.md).

## Notes for a Hipcamp host

Zoning comes first: most residential parcels would need rezoning to C-OR/C-TR.
